Operator
Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in listen only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the meeting over to your host for today's call, Ms. Stella Wang, JinkoSolar's Investor Relations. Please proceed.
Stella Wang
Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Stella, thank you. Operator, thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q2 and Q3 2025 earnings conference call. The company's results were released earlier today and available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on newswire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar, Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., Mr. Gener Miao, CMO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd., Mr. Pan Li, the CFO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., Mr. Charlie Cao, CFO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business, operations, and company highlights, followed by Mr. Miao who will talk about the sales and marketing, and then Mr. Pan Li who will go through the financials.
They will all be available to answer questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under the applicable law. Now it is my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead Mr. Li Xiande.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Yeah Sangan so for.
Stella Wang
Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
In the Q1, Q2, Q3 of 2025 our global module shipments totaled 61.9 GW, once again ranking number 1 worldwide driven by our outstanding product performance and strong presence in high value overseas markets. Growth margin improved sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters to 2.9% in the Q2 and 7.3% in the Q3. Net loss continue to narrow sequentially. We are pleased to see that our intensive efforts devoted to storage, R&D and products in the past 2 years that started to bear fruit gradually. In the Q1, Q2, Q3, our cumulative energy storage system, the ESS shipments exceeded 3.3 GWh, increasing significantly for 2 consecutive quarters. This combined with the rising share of overseas markets has helped the profitability of our energy storage business improvement noticeably.
Considering that energy storage products are the process of installation, commissioning, and acceptance, there will be a lag in revenue recognition in our financial statement. We are confident that as economics of scale accelerate and competitiveness continues to improve, our energy storage business will more than double next year. Its revenue contribution is expected to rise significantly and serves as a key driver of our overall gross margin expansion. In Q2 and Q3, we continued to keep module utilization rates at a reasonable level. Since Q3, prices of polysilicon wafers and cells have all risen and module prices showed some upward trends. Given that feed-in tariff in all provinces are still in the implementation phase, central and state owned enterprises need some time to recalculate their IR returns and adjust their business models for end projects.
It is expected that demand will take some time to release. However, we have seen some positive signals in the raw material segment supported by rising raw material prices. Module prices in overseas markets have also increased. The upgrade towards high power production capacity has become an important direction for accelerating industry high quality development. This technical upgrade also meets end customers demand for high power products to achieve more reliable investment returns. As an industry pioneer to upgrade existing TOPCon capacity through technology enhancements, we made steady progress in high power product upgrades in Q3. We have already delivered some high power products carrying a premium of $0.01 to $0.02 per watt compared to their conventional products. As upgrade of the third generation Tiger Neo product with maximum power of 670 W is completed.
We expect the shipment for portion of high power products to increase quarter-over-quarter next year, accounting for 60% or above in 2020.
Since market-based electricity reform has removed the mandatory energy storage requirements, China's energy storage industry is accelerating its market-oriented development. With the increasing gap between peak and off-peak electricity prices and the implementation of policies such as capacity pricing and capacity compensation independent energy storage projects in multiple provinces can achieve sound economic returns. Driven by both improving economics and a global energy transition, demand is increasing in Europe, Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Latin America. In the US a rapid expansion of AI data centers has led to unprecedented surge in electricity demand. Streaming domestic electricity supply, Solar-plus-storage has therefore emerged as a safer and more easily deployed solution. We expect global demand for energy storage to experience explosive growth driven by increasing renewable energy penetration and declining storage system costs.
This once again validates our strategic decision to invest in the energy storage business in line with our industry trends and it has helped us to build a long-term competitive advantage. As a leading enterprise in the PV sector we possess long established advantages in channels, brand reputation, and customer resources enabling us to provide a localized one-stop solar plus storage solutions. On the manufacturing side, we currently have 12 GWh of pack capacity and 5 GWh of battery cell capacity and continuously improve product performance through self-developed technological breakthroughs. On the market side, we focus on high-margin overseas markets, particularly utilities, bill, and industry and commercial projects. Although delivery cycles are relatively long, demand remains strong providing stable and sustainable growth momentum for the company's energy storage business.
In summary the global supply chain is reshaping. The balance between supply and demand is gradually improving. As technological upgrades accelerate industry high-quality development, the market share of high-power and high-value products will continue to expand and become a dominant force in market pricing. Market competition, particularly in project bidding, increasingly favors leading enterprises that demonstrate strong technological capabilities and long-term reliability. Resources such as bank financing are also concentrating towards leading enterprises, further strengthening their market share. The strong technological capabilities long-term reliability, and global diversification of our energy storage business, we are well positioned to further strengthen our competitiveness and benefit from the industry. Next upward cycle.
The 15th Five-Year Plan proposed accelerating the decarbonization of both the energy supply and the construction sectors. The National Development and Reform Commission, NDRC, and the National Energy Administration have also recently issued guidance on promoting renewable energy integration and power system regulation further emphasizing the critical role of energy storage in the construction of a new energy sector. We expect these matters will further strengthen the competitiveness of China's renewable energy sector and steer the industry back onto a healthy and rational development path.
Looking forward to Q4 and the full year, we will continue to actively respond to the industry's call for rational development by maintaining reasonable production levels and focusing on upgrading and transforming high-efficiency capacity. At the same time, we will proactively adapt to change changes in overseas policies to ensure sustainable supply for our customers. We will keep strengthening our competitive advantages in technology and global operations, achieve a balance between scale and profitability while consolidating our industry-leading position. We expect the total shipments including solar modules, cells and wafers to be between 85 GW to 500 GW for the full year of 2025 and yes, that shipment to be 6 GW average for the 4 years 2025.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Thank you Mr Li. Total shipments were 21.5 GW in Q3 with module shipments accounting for 93%. By the end of Q3 we became the first module manufacturer in the industry to achieve accumulative global module shipments of 370 GW with total cumulative shipments of Tiger Neo series, the parting 200 GW, the best selling module series in history in terms of geographic mix. In Q3 we focused on high value overseas markets with shipments accounting for over 65%, achieving strong growth in Asia Pacific emerging markets and Europe. Shipments to the US were nearly 1.3 GW in Q3 doubled sequentially against the backdrop of the electricity market report, customer demand for high power products continues to rise.
Our high power Tiger Neo 3.0 series with its bifaciality rate of 85% and excellent low light performance can generate stable electricity during storm, dust, and cloudy weather, effectively extending power generation hours. At the same time, in a market environment with increasing volatility in electricity spot prices, the outstanding power generation performance of Tiger Neo 3.0 enables more power generation during peak price depends periods in the morning and evening, creating higher yield and more reliable returns for clients. According to our outward field test data, in Chengdu, China under low light conditions such as storm and dust, Tiger Neo achieves a 7.2% gain compared to BC products and in Kagoshima, Japan Tiger Neo shows 10.79% used ATM over BC products in low light condition. In Q3 we delivered some high power products that carries $0.01 to $0.02 premium compared to conventional products.
We expect our high power Tiger Neo 3.0 product with maximum power of up to 671 W to be produced in large-scale next year, further strengthening our competitiveness. On the product side, we once again tossed the PV Tech Q3 2025 module tech capability Report with AAA rating, thanks to our solid operational capabilities, outstanding technological innovation, and strong recognition from global customers as one of the few enterprises to continuously maintain top-tier creditworthiness and technological strength in the global PV industry. In the latest release of BNEF Energy Storage Tier 1 list for Q 2025, we were recognized as Tier 1 energy storage provider for the seventh consecutive quarter. Our continuous efforts in sustainable development have also earned international recognition repeatedly.
In the recent MSCI ESG meeting, we were upgraded to an A rating, maintaining our position in the top tier of ESG performers in the global PV industry. Additionally, our S&P CSA score continued to improve from 2024, rising significantly to 78, far ahead of the industry. On the demand side we expect global PV demand to slightly contract in 2026 in China due to the implementation of Policy Reform 136, the pace of carrying out 15th Five-Year Plan, as well as industry self-discipline and anti-involution measures. Demand is expected to slightly decrease year-over-year in 2026. Markets outside China are generally expected to remain healthy in the mean to long term.
The urgent power demand from AI data center combined with most countries' commitments to reduce carbon emissions will jointly drive growth in this global deployment of clean energy and a new grid infrastructure over the next three to five years. The State Council Information Office recently released the White Paper of China's Action on Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality which emphasizes that energy storage is a key support for building a new type of power system and advocates actively developing the renewable energy storage solution. In the US, we are already seeing some tech giants deploying co-located or nearby solar plus storage at their data centers to meet rapidly growing electricity needs. We believe renewable energy plus energy storage has become an invisible and accelerating trend. We remain optimistic about the long-term prospects of the US market.
Although trade policies impose certain constraints on the manufacturing side, we have taken proactive measures and made early strategic deployments adjusting our manufacturing and supply chain in response to policy changes to provide US customers with long-term, stable, and reliable solutions. We are confident that leveraging our advantage in technology, innovation, high-power products, and global network, we can continue to satisfy our global clients' demand for clean safe, high-efficiency, and reliable integrated solar and storage solutions. We will also continue to improve our competitiveness in global markets.
Mengmeng Li
Investor Relation Director, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you, Gener. We are pleased that our focus on high performance products and high value markets, as well as our efforts in cost and expenses control, have delivered steadily improved financial results. Gross profit margin turned positive in Q2 and continued to improve by 4.4 percentage points in Q3. Net loss and adjusted net loss narrowed sequentially for two consecutive quarters. Operating cash flow was $340 million in Q3 improving significantly quarter-over-quarter. Operating cash flow is expected to be positive for the full year 2025. Moving to the details, in Q3 total revenue was $2.27 billion, down 10% sequentially and 34% year-over-year. The sequential decrease was mainly due to a decrease in the solar module shipment, and the year-over-year decrease was primarily due to a decrease in average selling price of solar modules.
Gross margin was 7.3%. The sequential improvement was mainly due to a lower unit cost product sold and year-over-year decrease was mainly due to the decrease in ASP of solar modules. Total operating expenses were $363 million, up to 36% sequentially and down 32% year-over-year. The sequential decrease increase was primarily due to an increase in the impairment of long-lived assets while the year-over-year decrease was mainly due to the decrease in shipping. Cost of solar module shipment decreased and the average freight rate declined during Q3 this year. Total operating expenses accounted for 16% of total revenues compared to 10.6% in Q2 and 15.4% in Q3 last year. Operating loss margin was 8.7% compared with operating loss margin of 7.7% in Q2 this year and operating profit margin of 0.3% in Q2 last year.
Moving to the balance sheet at the end of Q3, our cash and cash equivalents were $3.3 billion compared with $3.4 billion at the end of Q2 2025 and $3.2 billion at the end of Q3 2024. Air turnover days were 105 days compared with 97 days in Q2. Inventory turnover days were 90 days compared with 66 days in Q2 this year. At the end of Q3, total debt was $6.4 billion compared to $6.7 billion at the end of Q2. Net debt was $3.1 billion compared with $3.3 billion at the end of Q2 this year. Debt conditions improved sequentially. Let me go into more details of Q2. Total revenue was $2.51 billion compound up 30% sequentially and down 25% year-on-year.
The sequential increase was primarily due to increase in solar module shipments while the year-over-year decrease was mainly due to a decrease in ASP of solar modules. Gross margin was 2.9%. The sequential improvement was mainly due to a lower unit cost of products sold, while year-over-year decrease was mainly due to the decrease in ASP of modules. Total operating expenses were $266 million, down 24% sequentially and 50% year-over-year. The sequential decrease was mainly due to the reduced expected credit loss expense in Q2 while the year-over-year decreases were mainly due to three points.
A decrease in the impairment of loan leave assets, reduced expected credit loss expenses and decreased shipping cost as the average freight rate declined during Q2 this year, total operating expenses accounted for 10.6% of total revenues compared to 18.1% in Q1 2025 and 16.9% in Q2 2024. Operating loss margin was 7.7% compared to 20.7% in Q1 this year and 4.7% in Q2 last year. Moving to the balance sheet at end of Q2, our cash and cash equivalent was $3.4 billion compared with $3.77 billion at the end of Q1 this year and $1.9 billion at the end of Q2 last year. AI turnover days were 97 days compared with 111 days in Q1 this year, inventory turnover days were 66 days compared to 84 days in Q1. Our operating efficiency is improving.
At the end of Q2, total debt was $6.7 billion compared to $6.4 billion at the end of Q1. Net debt was $33.3 billion compared to $2.6 billion at the end of Q1 this year. This concludes our prepared remarks. We are now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel your request, please press Star2. If you are on a speaker phone, please pick up the handset to ask your question. Your first question comes from Philip Shen with Roth Capital Partners.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi everyone. Thank you for taking my questions. First one's on your gross margins. Can you share some color on what you see as the difference between yours and Canadian Solar? They reported recently 15%. You guys have Q3 gross margins at about 7%. And what was the main driver you think, for that underperformance? Can you provide some color on the storage and solar gross margin difference? Finally, what do you think margins look like for Q4? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Thanks, Philip. I think compared to up here, particularly the N-type solar, the gross margin difference is, you know the different revenue contribution from the energy storage business. If you look at the Jinko, you know, quarter by quarter, we did improve gross margin dramatically. It's coming from majority you know, the module business. For the energy storage sectors we did. I want to have a very, very positive update I think in the prepared remarks of Chairman Li. We think our energy storage business is ready for the dramatic growth in next year 2026. We are expecting significant and revenue contributions and gross margin expansions. You know the storage is really, you know, in supply shortage. This year we shift around 6 GWh, you know, shipments. The next year we expect to double, at least double.
In terms of revenue recognition different because, you know the revenue is recognized, you know, for the shipments with the final acceptance, it's a little bit delayed Q1 to Q2. And for the energy storage business, the gross margin is at decent level. We expect at least 15% to 20% gross margin. Looking forward, particularly for the ESS business out of China, and we target 70% to 80% the ESS business next year. In terms of revenue contribution from the energy storage business, we expect 10% to 15%. I mean the revenue from ESS business compared to the total revenues of JinkoSolar next year. So it's a very, you know, we are actually, we think our business is shifting from purely module business to module plus ESS next year.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Great. Charlie, thank you very much for the color. Can you share also a little more color on your view? You have given us some color on the storage market. You shared that next year could be 6 gigawatt hours. What might the geographic shipment mix be for 2026? How much to the US, how much to China, and then maybe Europe and others? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yeah. This year is 6 GWh. Next year is double. Okay. That is the total volume in terms of geographical distributions and long China, roughly we think 70%, 80%, including United States and United States. We are in discussion with a lot of potential customers and developing, and we believe, you know, step by step we are getting more and more orders from us, but we are, you know, getting a lot. We have strong pipelines, particularly I think from Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Got it. Okay, great. Thank you. Shifting over to one more question here on the Foreign Entity of Concern for the US FEOC. Can you help us understand you plan to. You have a big business shipping us, sorry shipping solar modules to the US now you plan to ship batteries also to the US. Can you help us understand how you plan to comply with Foreign Entity of Concern requirements for the US market? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yeah. Looking for the next year. We don't believe there's a lot of kind of impact, negative impact from the FEOC, let's say UFLPA compliance. We are seeing a lot of safe harbor projects particularly for the solar plus some storage projects. We committed to from long term. I think we reshape our supply chain globally, and we are exploring options for our solar module facilities in Florida. And we think from the long term there is going to be demand for both FEOC and non-FEOC, and we are in if there is some kind of development particularly for transforming our solar module facilities in the United States to the long failed entities, and we will let investors know. We have been in the process to discussion with potential investors.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Got it. Okay. Thank you, Charlie. I'll pass it on.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Welcome.
Operator
Our next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Hello, this is Alan. From Jefferies. Thanks for taking my question. So my first question is about the ESS business. Would like to know if there is any discussion with any of the AI data centers or hyperscaler clients and what type of demand are they requiring? Like are they more like 2 to 4 hours so.
Capability compatible demand or it's more like even longer hours of storage requirement. Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
We think the AI driven data center, you know is going to put a lot of demand for the global electricity from long term. In our ESS team is in discussion with potential pipelines, you know for the data center, including US, Europe, and including China. It's still, you know, it's, you know, in the progress and we believe we are able to reach a significant milestone early next year.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. Clear. Thanks. So in relation to the geographical breakdown, we'd like to know if the gross margin of ESS is similar across the regions or it should be higher in Europe or US. How do you see the margins in different regions that you operate?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Well, you mean ESS is margin different regions, right? Yeah, yeah. It's depending on different markets. China is still a little bit low but I think it's recovering a little bit. Yes, it's very competitive in China, but Europe and US is still. We think that there is a decent gross margin. The Middle East are little bit low and I think China and Middle East is ESS. The pricing, the competitiveness, and the margin is relatively low to other regions, but we think it's still very healthy and business. And next two years.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Yes. Would like to know on the cost side of ESS because I have noticed that the upstream raw materials are all the cost of raw materials are increasing or surging. Any plans to lock in any raw materials or how is your view on different raw materials like batteries or like even more upstream battery materials like lithium carbonate, etc.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yeah, yeah. Because the strong demand the materials like ingots and wafers, firstly, we have 5 gigawatts and battery cell capacities, which put us at the advantage. The second one, we partner with key materials and suppliers. And the second one, when we negotiate contract, we did anticipate some kind of material cost upwards. The combination, I think, is a little bit challenge, but we think we can manage and how to minimize the impact of the material. And the pricing.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. I think my next question is about the demand on the solar module market. How do you see the demand growth in next year for maybe both solar and ESS? Like what is the growth rate you see?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Yeah, for the demand side, definitely we should look in separately for both PV and BESS. Right. For PV side, I think we are in a conservative way. We are expecting more or less flat year in 2026 versus 2025. The main reason is because China demand, you know, we believe it will have a drop compared with 2025, which because the weight of China demand is so high in the global demand, which drive even with the other markets booming or other markets growth, we still expect the total demand of the globe in the PV industry for next year will be more or less flat year. However, when we look into the BESS, it is in a different scenario, right? With more and more renewable installed, the grid needs more security for the BESS contribution, definitely we are seeing a sharp increase for the BESS site.
That's why for the best we are still keeping optimistic opinion or expectation for next year's installation. If we need to quantify that, we think it will be at least a 25% increase for the best year-over-year.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thanks. Gener would like to know like what type of installation in China are you looking at? Because there are different numbers flowing around. Are you looking at low 200 or even below 200 GW in China?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
I'm not that conservative for China because when recently I visited a lot of our distributors and even installers in China in all the different provinces, I think most of them are still keeping optimistic for next year. Having said all those, I believe that it will be around, let's say module wise it will be around mid-200, let's say around 250 about. If we look into the grid connection number, it should be somewhere around low 200s.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Okay, that is very clear. Thanks a lot. I think my last question is on the buyback. Would like to know if the company would start buyback after the blackout period, which is basically this result. How is the pace of the buyback will look like? Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
You know, we monetized 3%, right? 8 shares. I think the end of October. In the past to get money out of China, after the regulatory approval, we have paid withholding tax. We expect to get the money by the end of this month and very soon. For the shareholder, you know, shareholder returns, we commit at least $100 million a year. And we had deferred dividend early this year. We bought some shares, certain shares. I think last quarter, you know, in the middle of this year, and after the window you know, after the earnings release, we plan to repurchase this year throughout the end of the year.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Is it, like how much shares have been purchased or will the company looking to basically buy all the remaining amount in the buyback program in the remaining one month?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yes, and I think we, you know, we plan to use the procedure as a monetization issue since the key, you know funding, which is available, and it's around $170, US$88 million. I think we, depending how the market move, we definitely, we will repurchase shares by the end of this year, and roughly, I think, this year you know, $100 million, and we had to get dividend, I think, 50, 60 minutes. That's our, you know the base plan.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
That's clear.
We will, yeah,
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
It's a year-over-year plan. Next year it's roughly the same plan.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see that clear. Thank you. Thanks Charlie.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Thank you.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press Star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Your next question comes from Rajiv Chaudhri with Sunsara Capital.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
Good morning. My first question is regarding your guidance for module shipments for Q4. You know it's a very big range, 18 to 33 GW. You have essentially kept to the same range that you gave for the full year back in early part of the year. Now we are halfway through Q4. Could you help us narrow down what the range would be for Q4 for module shipments?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Yeah, I think we will close to the lower end of the range. I think because of the regulatory requirement we have to keep that range as before. From the operational level we believe the lower end of the range is more let's say realistic.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
I see. Related to that, what do you think the global shipments of modules would be for the industry as a whole in 2025?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Well, we technically believe from the production wise, we are looking at roughly 700 gigawatts. That's the high-level numbers we are estimating for the whole industry.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
Do you believe that 700 gigawatts would actually have been shipped out by the industry as well or that was just the production?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Well, I think it is more realized to a production closer to the production side. Because every company has a strong, slightly different ways to calculate or announce their shipment numbers. That is why it's difficult to figure out what is the real shipment number. Production wise I think the number is more realistic.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
I see. Okay. So moving on to another question relating to CapEx. Could you give us the CapEx target for 2025 and also for 2026?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
It's roughly RMB 5 billion, you know, this year and next year. And by next year, we didn't have any, you know, plan to, you know, expand, you know, capacity. It's kind of upgraded to the next generation TOPCon technology. It's going to have significant, you know, high-end high power output solar modules we are able to provide to our customer next year, roughly 60%. With price premium and relatively good margin contributions. Next year, quarter-over-quarter, the capacity for the high-end upgraded high-end module capacity will be released quarter by quarter.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
So Charlie, just to be clear, this year the CapEx is 5 billion RMB and next year it will be flat at RMB 5 billion.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yes, roughly. Next year I talk about it. This year it's a roughly payment of outstanding, you know, amount, you know, RMB 5 billion. Next year we are doing the upgrade existing capacity and to the next high level, you know, TOPCon capacity. And we foresee a lot of strong demand and with higher module price and higher gross margin contributions.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
So you made a very interesting point that operating cash flow will be positive in 2025. It looks like you will be generating operating cash flow positive in 2026 as well and maybe substantially higher than 2025 because the gross margin will be higher. Is that a correct assessment?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
That's right, that's right. And we talk about firstly I think the catalyst is first one is ESS storage business. Next year, we are looking to 10% to 15% revenue contributions from ESS with decent gross margin and priority and net profitability. And second one is the module business. We have, I think, the most advanced TOPCon upgrade capacities in industries and developed by ourselves for the technology, which will roughly have 60% shipment of the modules coming from the next generation Jinko developed TOPCon capacities with higher gross margins.
Second one, we thinking from the high level standards, industry anti-involution, you know, taking the effect step by step. The capacity will accelerate, you know, phase out, and leading by the, you know, on top of that, industry leading self discipline, you know, control production volume and reasonable pricing based on the cost will take further, I think, enforcement. So combined together, I think the industry is reaching the low point, is recovering step by step, and Jinko, we are getting ready for the from the market and product perspective. Plus we are shifting solar plus ESS story and business. The basic plan next year, we are, you know, we are trying, we are confident that we are able to, you know, navigate the cycles and turn to positive earnings. That is kind of the, you know, the business plan next year.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
You talked about the premium products and the fact that they've got premium pricing. On the cost side, will your costs for these premium products will still be lower than the cost for the standard products this year? In other words, do the costs keep going down even as the price goes up?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Yes, yes, initially by design the cost is a little bit higher, but a very, very small, you know, incremental cost. By the way, our R&D team continue to, you know, to dive into the details and to try to, you know, further improve the cost. Back to your question. I think that, you know, the high-end product cost is very, very small incremental, you know cost, cost increase at the beginning. We believe over time, you know, our R&D team, with our operational teams, will continue to improve the cost.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
Final question Charlie, on market share. In the past, in 2023 and 2024, your global market share had gone up to somewhere between 15% and 16% of the global market. This year it is down a little bit, I guess partly because you have restrained production because of the pricing. Should we expect that your market share next year will go up again and maybe go up a lot more than 16% because the industry itself is consolidating. What do you think the range for next year module shipments could be.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
The consolidated market share after consolidation or, you know, the industry consolidation and the phase out of capacity, the industry you know, turn into the kind of normal situation is for sure. It's very good for tier one companies. If you look at the long term, we are confident and we will continue to penetrate the market share. The next year is still, I think, from the top down approach. I think China will continue to launch, implement the anti-involution policies. We don't expect significant shipments increase for the module business. Yes, it's different stories.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Analyst, Sunsara Capital
Okay, thank you very much.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Welcome.
Operator
Your next question comes from Philip Shen with Roth Capital Partners.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Thanks for taking my ball budget. I wanted to check back in with you. In terms of Q4 margin outlook, what kind of solar module ASP could we see in Q4 and then what kind of margin for the overall quarter could we see? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
We expect relatively stable Q4 versus Q3, but ESS business is contributing more revenues. We estimate our ESS business in Q4 is going to reach positive profitability levels, but the contribution is not significant. Next year is a different story we have talked about. And for the module business we expect relatively stable.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay, got it, thanks. And then can you talk about module ASPs for Q1 and Q2 of next year and then also the trajectory for margins as you blend in more battery? Thanks.
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Yeah, Phil, I think it's difficult to share those numbers or estimations right now because, you know, what is happening is like some of the key market, they are still, you know, there are, you know, some key or some important policy is upcoming. For example, you know, the US the guidance of the FEOC or material assistance or even upcoming 232, which will significantly impact the market prices. Like in China, you know, there is anti-involution policies and there is even more rumors coming out regarding the polysilicon even to the other part of the manufacturing value chain as well. Those changes could significantly change the market price overnight. That is why we believe it's still too early to share our estimation on the prices for next year.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay, Gener, that makes sense. You talked about the rumors on poly. Can you give us a little more color on that? Thanks.
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
I don't have too much more to share based on. There is a lot of rumors on the market or on the Internet. I don't know what you are referring to.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Yeah, I was just, you mentioned it. I thought I would try to see if there is more color.
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
We are not part of the game. I don't have too much to share with everyone. Thank you for your question.
Philip Shen
Managing Director, Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Yep, no problem. Okay, thank you guys. I'll pass it on.
Operator
Your next question comes from Brian Lee with Goldman Sachs.
Tyler Bisset
CFA, Goldman Sachs
Hey guys, this is Tyler Bisset on for Brian. Thanks for taking our question. Just quick housekeeping questions. Can you share what was D&A and CapEx in Q2 and Q3?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
You mean the absolute number percentage? Right? Hello?
[Company Representative] (JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.)
Company Representative, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Hello.
Tyler Bisset
CFA, Goldman Sachs
Yeah, sorry. Like the actual number,
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
I think in the financial statement. You got to check out, you know, the financial statement, the R&D, and the, you know, operating expenses. We have disclosed quarter-over-quarter. What would be your key question you want to explore?
Tyler Bisset
CFA, Goldman Sachs
Sorry, D&A and CapEx in Q2 and Q3. Like the absolute numbers.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
You mean depreciation or CapEx?
Tyler Bisset
CFA, Goldman Sachs
Yes, sorry.
Depreciation and CapEx.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Okay.
Depreciation by quarter I think is roughly, you know, and I think $300 million a quarter. And the CapEx, I think, is the first half year we, you know, spent roughly RMB 2 billion. Okay.
Tyler Bisset
CFA, Goldman Sachs
Okay, thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co., Ltd.
Okay.
Operator
That is our last question. That does conclude our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

content.text:
Operator
Conference call. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the meeting over to your host for today's call, Miss Stella Wang, JinkoSolar's Investor Relations. Please proceed, Stella.
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
Thank you, operator. Thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q1 2025 Earnings Conference Call. The company's results were released earlier today and available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on newswire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., Mr. Gener Miao, CMO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd., Mr. Pan Li, CFO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., and Mr. Charlie Cao, CFO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and company highlights, followed by Mr. Miao, who will talk about the sales and marketing, and then Mr. Pan, who will go through the financials.
They will be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements, except as required under the applicable law. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
Module shipments reached 17.5 GW, with revenues of $1.91 billion for Q1 2025. Prices across the main solar industrial chain were low in the Q1. This, combined with disruptions in demand caused by changes in international trade policies, pressured profit margins in each segment of the integrated solar supply chain. Despite this challenging market environment, we fulfilled our delivery commitment to our customers and reduced the cost through supply chain optimization, adjustments in production and operation plans, and other measures. Due to a year-over-year decline in shipments to the US market and a continued decline in higher priced overseas orders, our module prices and profitability decreased both year-over-year and sequentially in Q1. Net loss was approximately $180 million for Q1.
According to data from the NEA, new installations in China in Q1 amounted to 59.7 GW, an increase of 31% year-over-year. Resilience was seen in domestic demands despite the higher comparison base in 2024. Market self-regulation and high-quality development initiatives by manufacturers were gradually effective. From January to March, average monthly bidding prices for solar modules steadily recovered in the domestic market. The bidding prices returned to a more rational level. Recently, as the policy cut-off deadlines for distributed solar regulations and market-based renewable price reform on 30 April and 31 May approach, market sentiment has cooled down to some extent, and the distributed module prices have fallen back from their previous highs. At the same time, changes in international trade policies such as reciprocal tariffs in the United States have continued to bring certain disruptions to the PV industry.
In response to these challenges, we have flexibly adjusted our supply chain strategy and regional shipment mix while maintaining close communication and negotiation with our customers. Relying on our extensive market insights and efficient execution, we remain committed to meeting customer demand for our high efficient and reliable products. Maintaining operations continually while adapting to market dynamics. Currently, visibility of our order book stands at 60% to 70%, with Indo-Pacific and the Middle East and Africa exceeding 80%.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
Cost reduction and increasing efficiency remain the mainstay in the development of the PV industry, and customers' demand for higher power products is growing rapidly to further reduce LCOE. Due to limitations in the upgrading and the transformation of most conventional TOPCon capacity in the industry, differences between manufacturers in TOPCon cell efficiency, product performance, and cost are gradually widening. We believe that companies with high efficiency cell capacity and high-power products will have a competitive advantage in the market.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
By the end of Q1, the mass-produced cell efficiency for our third generation TOPCon products exceeded 26.6%. We continued to upgrade existing TOPCon capacity with the introduction of technologies such as the half-cell passivation, max and the 20 best part. We expect the power of our third generation TOPCon products to have a 20 W to 30 W advantage compared to previous generation TOPCon products in the industry. Meanwhile, we kept making breakthroughs in our R&D. By the end of Q1, our laboratory efficiency for perovskite tandem solar cells based on TOPCon reached 34.22%, once again setting a new record.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
Our investments in R&D, manufacturing, and after-sale service capabilities in energy storage are gradually showing results. In Q1, shipments of our ESS exceeded 300 MWh, a large increase compared to the same period last year. We expect shipments of our ESS to be around 6 GWh for the full year 2025, with the overseas market as our strategic priority. Confirmed orders for energy storage systems accounted for 50% to 60%, with another 20% to 30% showing strong potential for signing. Leveraging our leading position in the PV industry, we will proactively explore innovative business models that integrate solar and storage solutions, providing high efficiency and smart green energy solutions to global clients and contributing to the sustainable development of the global energy.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding
Before turning over to Gener Miao, I would like to go over our guidance for Q2 and the full year 2025. We set our annual production capacity for mono wafers, solar cells, and solar modules to reach 120, 95, and 130 GW respectively, with annual production capacity of our third-generation TOPCon modules to reach 40 to 50 GW by the end of 2025. We expect module shipments to be between 20 to 25 GW in Q2 2025 and between 85
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding
To 100 GW for the full year 2025. We will actively respond to changes in market demand and the policy, continuously optimize market strategies and supply chain management, and consistently improve technology and product competitiveness to maintain a leading position in the industry.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding
Thank you, Pan Li. Q1 total shipments were 19.1GW, with module shipments accounting for approximately 90%. Although demand was impacted by the off-season, we sustained the industry's highest shipment levels by leveraging our global sales network and the strength of our products. Shipments to overseas markets accounted for around 70%. We proactively embraced the surge in the demand in the Indo-Pacific and the North Asia markets. Shipments to Indo-Pacific market grew by nearly 10% year-over-year, and 150% sequentially, while shipments to North Asia increased by nearly 20% year-over-year. US shipments accounted for approximately 5% in line with our guidance. On the product side, customer demand for our third generation high-power TOPCon products continued to grow.
Our third generation high-power TOPCon is expected to have a mainstream output over 650 Wp, with a maximum of 670 Wp. Thanks to lower degradation, lower temperature coefficient, higher bifaciality, and enhanced reliability, it can deliver better power generation yields for end customers. Currently, customers are willing to pay a premium for such high power generation. Recently, we were once again recognized as a Tier 1 energy storage provider by Bloomberg. We have been listed in the BloombergNEF ranking for four consecutive quarters. A strong recognition from a third party and customers of our safe and reliable energy storage solution, as well as our timely delivery and deployment capabilities.
With the increasing economics of integrated solar and storage solutions and the continued expansion in the application scenarios, particularly against the backdrop of high energy consumption driven by AI, integrated solar and storage solutions are increasingly becoming feasible. The overseas market has always been one of our strengths. In 2025, we will further expand the energy storage business globally while continuing to focus on and explore technological innovation and application in specific application scenarios. We believe that the synergy between our solar and storage business will further increase our market competitiveness. On the demand side, we expect global module demand to remain about 700GW in 2025, with strong growth in Asia Pacific, Europe, and Middle East.
Following the recent rush installation in China with initiation of utility-scale projects in August and September, the overall demand is expected to continue to be in line with module supplies under the industry high-quality development initiatives. In the US, due to current shortage in local cell production capacity and the impact of reciprocal tariffs, there is likely to be a wave of early purchases of cells and modules. We remain optimistic about the long-term demand in the US market. In addition to the announced Saudi projects and existing US domestic operations, we are actively pursuing diverse solutions to strengthen our position in this market to enhance our long-term competitiveness.
We are confident that our extensive sales network and deeply localized customer services system will help us respond to the market dynamics, make flexible adjustments, and continue to satisfy customers' demand for more high efficient, reliable, and sustainable products. Pan Li.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding
Thank you, Gener Miao. During the challenging Q1, we continued to control costs and expenses, leading to a significant year-over-year decrease in comprehensive costs and operating expenses. In addition, we continued to optimize our asset-liability structure, as well as cash reserves. By the end of Q1, our asset-liability ratio was approximately 74%, lower than nearly 75% at the end of Q1 last year. By the end of Q1, our cash and cash equivalents were CNY 3.77 billion, a significant increase from CNY 2.44 billion at the end of Q1 last year. We will continue to optimize our asset-liability structure and maintain healthy cash reserves in 2025, further strengthening our resilience to risks. Let me go into more details now.
Total revenue was $1.9 billion, down 33% sequentially and down 40% year-over-year. The sequential decrease was primarily due to a decrease in shipments of solar modules. The year-over-year decrease was also due to a decrease in average selling price of modules. Gross margin decreased both sequentially and year-over-year, mainly due to the decrease in ASP of solar modules. Total operating expenses were $350 million, down 8% sequentially and down 18% year-over-year. The sequential decrease was mainly due to the decrease in the impairment of long-lived assets and a decrease in the losses resulting from disposal of long-lived assets. The year-over-year decrease was primarily due to the decrease in shipping costs as we shipped fewer solar modules.
Total operating expenses accounted for 18% of total revenues, compared to 13% in Q4 last year, and 13% in Q1 last year. Operating loss margin was about 20%, compared with 9% in Q4 last year and 1.5% in Q1 last year. Moving to the balance sheet. At end of Q1, our cash and cash equivalents were CNY 3.77 billion, compared with CNY 3.8 billion at the end of Q4 and CNY 2.44 billion at the end of Q1 last year. AR turnover days were 111 days, compared with 80 days in Q4 and 100 days in Q1 of last year.
Inventory turnover days were 84 days, compared with 57 days in the Q4 and 89 days in the Q1 of last year. At the end of the Q1, total debt was CNY 6.4 billion, compared to CNY 5.5 billion at the end of the Q4. Net debt was CNY 2.6 billion, compared to CNY 1.7 billion at the end of the Q4 last year. This concludes our prepared remarks. We are now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Your first question comes from Brian Lee with Goldman Sachs & Co.
Tyler Bisset
Equity Research Associate, Goldman Sachs
Hey, guys, this is Tyler Bisset for Brian. Thanks for taking our questions. Appreciate the ESS guidance of 6 GWh, and wondering if you can give a little bit more details on kinda where these shipments are going. Is this more in line with your module shipments today? I'm also curious where you guys are sourcing your battery cells.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding
It's mainly dominant. The ESS shipments makes it mainly dominated by Asia Pacific region, Europe region, and emerging markets. Well, those together with China, those four regions are our main target in terms of 2025. Which is slightly different from what we have for modules. For the key markets, it's very, let's say it's a very, very similar to each other. In terms of the geographic mix because of the trade barrier in US, et cetera. It is difficult to extend the ESS business in US right now.
Tyler Bisset
Equity Research Associate, Goldman Sachs
Thank you. Given the final determination on AD/CVD, which was, I guess, relatively more favorable for Malaysia, how are you thinking about your future imports to the US? Could you see that potentially increasing at all, or do you think it's more likely to stay in the 5% range?
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding
Well, I think the AD/CVD is only a preliminary tariffs. They still have what they call sunset termination after 12 months of customs clearance, which brings the company a lot of uncertainty. In that case, we are trying to look into the different options we have in order to provide more certainties and providing more competitive in terms of the cost as well. Right now, we are still working hard for the short term because the recent hike or change on the AD/CVD together with trade barriers is pretty new. In long term, we still have our commitment to the US market with our strategy in the joint venture factories in Middle East, together with our local operation in the US. We are still fully committed.
Tyler Bisset
Equity Research Associate, Goldman Sachs
All right. Thank you very much.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Philip Shen with Roth Capital Partners.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi, everyone. Thanks for taking my questions. So you guys had negative gross margins for the first time in a long time in Q1. I was wondering if you can talk through what you expect for margins for Q2 and Q3. Then, when do you expect the margins to go back positive? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
The gross margin to negative is very extreme cases in the last five years. It's reflecting the supply and demand imbalance throughout last year. On top of that, Q1 is the slack season, and we have more exposures to the China market. We expect, in short term, the gross margin to improve slightly in Q2 given the module price is in upward trend with the pushed demands from China and other regions. In the H2 year, we expect it to be stable, maybe have the chance to improve.
We believe the current situation is not sustainable even for the top-tier companies. From supply side, we are seeing more and more companies phase out in the solar industries. On top of that, there's uncertainties on international trade. We believe, you know, by the end of this year, we have more clarifications. Thank you.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Thank you, Charlie. Shifting to the US market, there is the 145% tariff. I wanted to understand what are the updates on your plans to ramp up US cell manufacturing in Florida or wherever that might be. Also, with the 145% tariff, are you able to import solar cell tools without. Like, is there an exemption for the tools, or is there no exemption for the tools, so it makes the ramping of US cell manufacturing more difficult? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. I think it may become one of the board, you know, questions. From the long-term belief, we believe, you know, local production in the US for local customers in the United States is a trend that is consistent with, I think, you know, the long-term policies from the current Trump administration. Short-term, there's a lot of uncertainties. There's the budget cuts, there's IRA incentive. There is maybe what we are interested in the [FLOC], you know, kind of this kind of things. While we take our approaches, we consistently evaluate the policies from the different angles.
As long as there is some kind of certainty, and we strongly believe US solar market will just boom, you know, next year. Specifically for the, you know, if we want to build the solar cell facilities, and we import the equipment from China under the current, you know, tariff, it's a crazy risk, right? It doesn't make sense to make the decisions even from that specific angles. Back to your question, Sandra. We don't have the plan in the short term, you know, solar cell we build in the US. We have, you know, the plan consistently evaluate the policies, the potential size or the potential, you know, the tariff situations.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Thank you very much. I'll pass it on.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Welcome.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Your next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you for taking my question. This is Alan. My first question is, it is the first time I think the company have provided the guidance on ESS. Would like to know if there's any indication on the margins on ESS, like some ballpark range, because ESS has been quite competitive in the Middle East as well.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Oh, you mean the margin, right?
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Yeah.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
The margin was.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Yeah. Gross margin.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Yeah. Gross margin. I think we target 5% to 10%. It's not very, you know, big target. Given, you know, the business we developed, you know, and starting from the kind of the very small scale. Last year we achieved 1GW, but this year we have the confidence to penetrate the market, particularly in, you know, Asia Pacific, you know, North America or some emerging markets. So the profitability is not the first priorities. But in terms of gross margin, we expect, you know, in the kind of the range of 5% to 10%.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
5% to 7%, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
5% to 10%.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Okay. Thank you. My next question is about... Did the company receive IRA credits for the production last year at this point in time, or if the company has sold any of the IRA 45X credits already.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
In last year, I think we filed, you know, the filings and the, you know, the kind of the deduction of the, you know, tax payable, you know, for the facilities. This year we are exploring the opportunities and to sell the credit to the outside investors, and it's in the process.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
You managed to get the credits already, just managing to sell it to financial institutions, right? For this year.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. This year we plan, you know, it's because, you know, we have 2 GW in full operations and well, there's a lot of, you know, potential investors who are interested, you know, to procure the credit from the facilities. We are in the process of the communication and negotiation.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you. So, another question is, what is the US shipment target, approximately for this year? Because there's a lot of changes since last time we talked. Is there already some inventory in the US to support that shipment?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
You know, the range is 5% to 10%, but you're right. Uncertainty, I think, is the big headwind. I think, if the, you know, headwind in uncertainty is, you know, will not be as, let's say, clear in the short term, it will have the impact on the shipments to the US. But I think 5%, you know, it's kind of the base and, let's say, the low case, but we are confident that we can achieve at least 5%. If the uncertainty is, you know, it's kind of the to be, you know, to have more clarity than the.
There is, you know, available supply chain to the US, and we can ship more. Again.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
5% of total shipment, right? Like, if it's 85 to 100 giga for this year, it's around 45 giga.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yes. Roughly. Yes.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. Thank you. My last question is on the shareholders' return program. I think after the announcement of Q4 result and Q1 result now, I wonder if the company can start buying back the shares, given the shares actually have also went down quite a bit. What the pace of the buyback will look like.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Well, after you know the release of the you know Q1, we plan to buy back from the market. We think it's a good timing given the valuation is very low. On top of that, we plan to declare dividends, but which is subject to further approval. It's on, I think, on our you know the schedule.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
To my understanding, the dividends will be approximately like $50 million, right? If it's around $1 per share, say for example. Would the buyback will be look like $150 million then?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
We have not decided, you know, but it's roughly, I think, at least CNY 100 million. You know, we split into the dividend plus the repurchase. This is the first step. Now, I think we communicate previously, we like to monetize the financial investment, you know, for some companies which was listed in recent years. On top of that, we may explore, you know, other options to monetize some assets from the US holding perspective.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. Before that happens, actually you can already start and there's at least 100 million, which is like 10% of the outstanding shares, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. CNY 100 million, I think it's kind of include, you know, dividend and plus the repurchase here. That's, you know, the plan.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I hear. After you liquidate some of your financial assets, there may be upside to this CNY 100 million dividend plus buyback.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
We may increase, but depending on how or the timing and how, you know, quick we can monetize the assets.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thanks a lot. I will pass on. Thank you, Charlie.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. That's star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced if you have any questions. Your next question comes from Rajiv Chaudhri with Sunsara Capital.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Hello, Charlie. The first question is about the market share. You mentioned that this year the market might go to about 700 GW, and last year it was a little bit around 600+. I'm wondering, you know, if even if you do the high end of your range, which is 100 GW, your market share looks like it might be lower than last year and lower than 2023. Could you clarify that discrepancy?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
I think last time we talked about, you know, our strategy is not to increase or, you know, penetrate more market share under the, you know, the imbalance of the supply and demand side, and particularly the industry is losing the money. What we are doing is we want to be flexible in the total shipments and which we guided under 85 to 100 GW. What it means is we want to balance the utilization, shipment and profitabilities, and as well as the cash flow, you know, perspective. On top of that, we need to, you know, to select the customers. We have a lot of, you know, potential customers and, you know, interest orders, but we need to be more selective.
For the long term, I think last time we talked about we target at least 20% the market share, you know, for the module business. It's not a one night target, you know. We need to focus our product competitiveness. We continue to invest in R&D and, you know, penetrate the key market with some kind of premium, make sure, you know, the business is sustainable.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Okay. Thanks. Along the same lines on the market growth, can you talk about, you know, where, which regions, geographic regions are going to get the 100 GW of growth from last year? How much growth do you expect in China and the US, for example, and also in Europe and India?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Sure. I can roughly talk about it. At the top level, we are looking at the global demand at roughly 700GW. Of which the largest market is believed to be China, same as last year. One side is that China is expected to grow roughly 10 to 15%, and which will account for around 45% of the global demand. The second largest after China is believed to be, we say Europe, the pan-Europe region. The whole Europe will be over 100GW level. I think that the only two markets pass the 100GW threshold in 2025.
For sure there are other markets, so very interesting and sizable, such as the US. We are roughly looking at 50 to 55 GW level. India, we are looking at around 30 to 35 GW level. That's all the big numbers, you know, in mind. For sure the attractive growth is mainly coming from the emerging markets, for example, the Asia Pacific region, and also the African regions. Because of the low base from last year, the growth rate is pretty high. If you look into the absolute growth numbers in terms of the GW, definitely the top four markets, which I just mentioned, are still the key focus.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Just to clarify, so you're expecting that China will grow by 10 to 15% this year?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
10 to 15, yes.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
I see. Okay. A final question. Are you still getting a premium pricing for your TOPCon products based on the technology?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
It depends on which technology or which product you are comparing with, right? Definitely from the customer end, as long as the product is generating more power output or technically more yield, more IRRs returns, customer are more than happy to pay premium on such kind of product.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
I see. Can you also give the breakdown you expect between the DG and the utility scale for this year for Jinko?
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Strategically, we lower the DG numbers a little bit, based on the price trend. Last year, the DG ratio is roughly close to high 40. Close to 40. 50, but the high 40, so let's say 47, 46. This year, the number will go down to roughly 30 to 35 range.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
I see. Okay.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
For this year.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder, President, and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO and Deputy General Manager, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Thank you.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. That is one last call for questions. Star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. We are showing no further questions at this time. Thank you for your attendance today. That does conclude our conference. You may now disconnect.
