content.text:
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you, operator. Thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. The company's results were released early today and available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on Newswires services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited, Mr. Gener Miao, CMO of JinkoSolar Company Limited, Mr. Pan Li, CFO of JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited, and Mr. Charlie Cao, CFO of JinkoSolar Company Limited. Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and company highlights, followed by Mr. Gener Miao, who will talk about the sales and marketing, and then Mr. Pan Li, who will go through the financials.
We will all be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under the applicable law. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
很高兴凭借在N-type TOPCon的技术、全球化运营和一体化产能等方面的优势，我们在充满挑战的2023年取得了非常亮眼的运营和财务业绩。感谢晶科团队非常强的执行力，全年组件出货量同比增长76.4%，达到了78.5吉瓦，重回行业第一。得益于我们在成本优化方面所做的努力，全年的盈利水平取得了同比大幅提升。全年毛利率为16%，相比2022年的4.8%。净利润为US$4.856亿，同比增长4.56倍。经调整后，利润为US$5.736亿，同比增长1.93倍。四季度组件出货量26.3吉瓦，超出了我们的指引。由于四季度全行业组件价格出现超预期的下跌，我们有接近50%的组件销往价格较低的中国市场。四季度毛利率为12.5%，环比三季度19.3%有明显下滑。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
We are pleased to have achieved very impressive operational and financial results in a challenging year by leveraging our advantages in N-type TOPCon technology, globalized operations, and integrated capability. Thanks to strong execution by our team, our module shipments for the full year increased 76.4% year-over-year to 78.5GW, back to the top position in the industry. Benefiting from our efforts in cost optimization, our profitability for the full year improved significantly year-over-year. Gross margin at 16% compared to 14.8% in 2022. Net income was $485.8 million, up 4.56x year over year. Adjusted net income was $573.8 million, up 1.93x year over year. Module shipments in Q4 was 26.3GW, exceeding our guidance.
As module prices fell more than expected in Q4 and nearly 50% of our modules were sold to the Chinese market at lower prices. Growth margin for Q4 was 12.5%, a significant decline from 19.3% in Q3.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
2023年国内光伏新增装机达到了216.88吉瓦，同比增长了148.1%，再创历史新高。与此同时，产业链各环节的供需失衡导致了价格下跌。组件中标价格年底较年初下降了超过40%，跌破了RMB 1元每瓦。2023年光伏产品的出口量同比大幅增长，但由于价格下跌，出口额同比小幅下跌。今年一月和二月需求淡季叠加部分厂商的恶性竞争，加剧了市场恐慌和价格的非理性。晶科面对低价竞标，保持了谨慎和理性。此外，一些不具备成本和产品竞争力的厂商纷纷减产或者停产，我们的开工率仍维持在行业领先的水平。三月，随着需求回暖和库存去化，组件价格逐渐企稳，部分招标价格有所回升。但中期来看，组件价格的下降将显著提升光伏的经济性。预计2024年全球光伏市场需求会持续增长。同时新的技术快速迭代和老旧产能的淘汰也会加速行业的整合。TOP10组件企业的市场占有率有望从2023年的70%提升到2024年的90%以上。我们有信心在这一轮周期波动中不断增强竞争力。预计2024年晶科的市场占有率将会有进一步的增长。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
In China, newly added PV installation reached 216.88GW in 2023, up 148.1% year-over-year to a historical high. At the same time, excess supply in various links of the industrial chain led to price declines. Tender prices for modules at the year-end decreased over 40% to below CNY 1 per watt. Compared to the beginning of the year, export volumes of PV products in 2023 increased significantly year over year, whereas export volume fell slightly as a result of decreasing prices. In January and February 2024, seasonality combined with extreme competition from certain manufacturers intensified market panic and irrational prices. We remain cautious and rational in the face of abnormally low tenders.
In addition, while some manufacturers without competitive cost or advanced products reduced or suspended production, we maintained our leading utilization rates in the industry as a result of a cost advantage and high order visibility. Into March, as demand picked up and inventory reduced, module prices gradually stabilized, and some bidding prices rebounded slightly. In the short- to mid-term, we expect the decline in module price will significantly improve the economics of solar energy, and we anticipate demand in the global PV market will continue to increase in 2024. Meanwhile, rapid iteration of new technologies and the elimination of obsolete production capacity will also accelerate the consolidation of the industry. Market share for the top 10 module manufacturers is expected to increase from 70% in 2023 to over 90% in 2024.
We are confident to consistently enhance our competitiveness through cyclical fluctuations, and we expect our market share to further increase in 2024. Thanks to our integrated manufacturing strategy and a leading position in N-type TOPCon technology in the early stage. By the end of Q4, our N-type capacity exceeded 70GW and our cost structure continues to improve. Currently, our mass produced N-type cell efficiency exceeds 26%, while the integrated cost of N-type is almost on par with P-type. With the continuous introduction of new cell technologies and optimization of cost reducing process, our cost structure is expected to become more competitive. We attach great importance to intellectual property rights and are fully focused on sustaining our technical leadership based on extensive intellectual property rights. By the end of the Q4, we had been granted 330 TOPCon patents.
One of the largest portfolios of granted TOPCon patents in the world. With the largest overseas integrated capacity of over 12GW in the industry and an effective supply chain traceability system, we have become the most reliable module supplier to the US market, which is expected to generate significant profits in 2024. Furthermore, our investment in innovative production model is expected to generate returns over time. Phase 1 and 2 of our integrated projects in Shanxi will start production in H1 2024 as planned, and gradually ramp up in H2. The full integration of automation can greatly improve labor efficiency and operation turnover efficiency, and is expected to bring a significant reduction in operating costs after reaching full production.
In the mid to long term, the rapid expansion of AI and electric vehicles may lead to tight power supply in the world, and the demand for clean power generation is expected to further increase. So far, reduced solar cost has significantly increased the competitiveness of solar in energy sectors. In the future, solar as a new quality productive force is set to play an increasingly important role in the face of energy crisis and energy transformation. We're bullish about PV market growth in the mid to long term, and we are confident we will continue to lead the industry with advanced technologies and a premium high efficiency product.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
考虑到供应量和市场情况，2024年的投资强度相对于2023年有明显下降。我们专注于先进N型产能的投资，包括山西大基地一体化N型产能28个吉瓦和越南N型电池和组件产能约4吉瓦。公司将致力提高运营资本效率和实现经营现金流的可持续增长。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Taking into account supply chain and market conditions, we are reducing investments in capacity expansion in 2024. We are focusing on expanding our advanced N-type capacity, including 28GW of integrated capacity in our Shanxi plant and about 4GW of N-type cell and module capacity in Vietnam. We continue to focus on improving working capital efficiency and achieving sustainable growth in operating cash flow.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
在把话题交给Gener之前，我来介绍一下业绩指引。预计2024年底，N型电池量产效率将达到26.5%。单晶硅片、高效电池、组件的产能分别达到120个吉瓦、110个吉瓦和130个吉瓦，其中N型产能占比90%以上。2024年第一季度组件出货量在18个吉瓦到20个吉瓦之间。2024年全年组件出货量100个吉瓦到110个吉瓦之间，其中N型出货量占比接近90%。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Before turning over to Gener, I would like to go over our guidance for Q1 and the full year of 2024. By the end of 2024, we expect mass produced N-type cell efficiency to reach 26.5%. We expect our annual production capacity for mono wafers, solar cells, and solar modules to reach 120GW, 110GW, and 130GW respectively by the end of 2024, this N-type capacity accounting for over 90% of total capacity. We expect the module shipments to be in the range of 18GW to 20GW for Q1 of 2024 and 100GW to 110GW for the full year 2024. This N-type accounting for nearly 90% of total module shipments.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
Gener.
Gener Miao
Chief Marketing Officer, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Thank you, Mr. Li. We are pleased to have achieved a historical high in quarterly and annual module shipments, thanks to our excellent global marketing network and the power of our product. Total shipments were 27.9GW in the Q4, with module shipment accounting for approximately 95%. Annual module shipment increased 76.4% year over year to 78.5GW. Both module shipments in the Q4 and the full year 2024 ranked world number one. We continued to improve product quality and build our customer service network to expand the influence of our brand. By the end of Q4, our accumulated global module shipment exceeded 210GW, covering more than 190 countries and regions.
In terms of geographic mix, China and Asia Pacific became our major shipment regions in Q4, accounting for approximately 70%. For the full year 2023, shipment to Asia Pacific and North America grew significantly, more than doubling year-over-year. As we continue to expand our footprint in overseas markets and build our integrated capacity, we move on to invest in North America and emerging markets. Based on our business conditions and market trends, China and Europe will continue to be the major contributor to the shipment in 2024, with North America, emerging markets, and Asia Pacific expected to flourish. On the product front, the competitive high-efficiency Tiger Neo accounted for 70% of the shipment in Q4, with average premium of CNY 0.10 per watt versus P-type modules.
The Tiger Neo accounted for approximately 60% of annual global shipments, achieving the goal we set at the beginning of the year and accelerated its market penetration globally. Currently, the power output of Tiger Neo modules is more than 30W higher than that of the similar P-type module, providing our customers with higher power generation yield. Shipments of our Tiger Neo were expected to account for over 85% in Q1 2024, and its product strength to continue to lead the industry. We are always committed to bringing greater economic value to our customer with high efficiency, highly reliable product and sustainable solutions. Recently, we unveiled the first Neo Green panels produced with renewable energy. These panels were produced in factories that were awarded the Zero Carbon Factory certification by TÜV Rheinland.
JinkoSolar is also the first company in the industry to be awarded with Zero Carbon Factory certification by TÜV for silicon ingot manufacturing, wafer cutting, cell manufacturing, and module manufacturing. We also continue to improve our ESG practices and optimize our traceability system. In the first quarter, we were awarded with the ESG Transparency Award from EUPD Research, which has recognized our far reaching commitment to sustainability and transparency. Recently, bidding for some domestic projects began to activate. EU inventories became depleted, and we have seen additional demand, especially in DG business. This gradually improved the PV economics and the growing demand for transmission to clean energy globally. PV demand in the global market is expected to further increase in 2024, but at a relatively slower pace than in 2023.
In longer term, the requirement of AI for computing power, which will further increase the demand for electricity and electrical equipment, ensuring strong growth potential for PV plus storage. As a responsible global company, we are always committed to providing clients with reliable and highly efficient product and solution, practicing the values we shared with our clients, partners, and investors to accelerate to a greener future. With that, I turn the call over to Pan.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited
Thanks to solid execution of our operations and management strategies, as well as successful efforts in cost optimization, we delivered excellent financial performance. For the full year, key metrics such as total revenues, gross margins, income from operations, and net income all significantly increased year-over-year. We also improved working capital efficiency and optimized operating cash flow. By the end of Q4, we had cash and cash equivalents of CNY 2.75 billion, and our net debt decreased by over 20% year-over-year. In December, we announced the extension of our existing share repurchase program. By the end of February this year, we had repurchased nearly 1 million ADSs in aggregate amount of approximately $28 million.
With our advantages in N-type TOPCon technology, globalized operations, and integrated capacity, we are very confident in our growth prospect, and we will continue to improve working capital efficiency and achieve sustainable growth in operating cash flow. Let me go into more details now. Total revenue was CNY 4.6 billion, an increase of 3% sequentially and more than 9% year-over-year. Gross margin was 12.5% compared with 19% in Q3 and 14% in Q4 2022. The decreases were mainly due to the decrease in average selling prices of solar modules. Total operating expenses were CNY 526 million. The increases were mainly attributed to loss on disposal of PPE and expense in relation to settlement of a dispute with customers. Operating margin was 1.1% compared with 2% last year.
Excluding the impact from a change in fair value of the notes and long-term investments and share-based compensation expenses, adjusted net income attributable to JinkoSolar Holding Company ordinary shareholders was CNY 65 million, compared with CNY 45 million in the Q4 last year. Up 73% year-over-year. Now I'll brief you on our 2023 full year financial results. Total module shipments were 78.5GW, up 76% year-over-year, and total revenues up 43% year-over-year. For the full year 2023, gross profit was about $2.7 billion, an increase of 55% year-over-year. Gross margin was 16% compared to 14.8%. The increase was mainly attributed to the decrease in the material cost of solar modules. Total operating expenses were CNY 1.8 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
The increase was mainly due to an increase in impairment loss on PPE, an expense in relation to settlement of dispute with customer, and an increase in staff cost. Operating margin for the full year of 2023 was 5% compared to 0.5% last year. Excluding the impact from a change in fair value of notes, long-term investments, and share-based compensation expenses, adjusted net income attributable to JinkoSolar Holdings ordinary shareholders was about CNY 574 million, up nearly 2x year-over-year. Let's move into the balance sheet. As mentioned, at the end of Q4, our cash and cash equivalents were significantly higher at
CNY 2.75 billion, half from CNY 1.93 billion at the end of Q3 and CNY 1.64 billion at end of Q4 2022. AR turnover days were down to 76 days in Q4 from 87 days in Q3. Inventory turnover days were down to 57 days from 67 days in Q3. Total debt was CNY 4.38 billion at year-end, compared to CNY 4 billion last year. Net debt was CNY 1.6 billion compared to CNY 2.3 billion last year. This concludes our prepared remarks. We're now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel your request, please press star two. Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Okay, great. Thank you very much. Good luck in 2024.

content.text:
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you, operator. Thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q3 2023 earnings conference call. The company's results were released earlier today and available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on news wire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman of the Board of Directors and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. Mr. Gener Miao, Chief Marketing Officer of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd. Mr. Pan Li, Chief Financial Officer of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., and Mr. Charlie Cao, Chief Financial Officer of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and company highlights, followed by Mr. Miao, who will talk about the sales and marketing.
Mr. Pan Li, who will go through the financials. They will all be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor Provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under the applicable law. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
[Non-English content]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
We are pleased that we were able to overcome the challenges we faced due to market volatility and deliver a strong Q3. We did so by leveraging our advantages in N-type TOPCon technology, extensive global operation network and advanced integrated capacity structures. Our module shipments, gross margin and net income all increased significantly year-over-year. Total module shipments were approximately 21.4 GW, an increase of 107.9% year-over-year. Polysilicon costs decreased sequentially. High-efficiency N-type products that command a premium account for over 60% of total module shipments. Module shipments to the US market recorded sequential growth in the Q3, all contributing to improve the profitability. Year-over-year, our net income increased by 140.7% to $181.4 million.
Adjusted net income increased by 215.1% to $184.6 million. Diluted earnings per ordinary share increased by 188.7% to $0.63. Gross margin increased from 15.7% to 19.3%.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
[Non-English content]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Since Q3, price declines in the supply chain have stimulated end market demand. For the first nine months, newly added installations of PV in the domestic market reached 128.9GW, nearly 50% more than the full-year installations in 2022. As one of the new three products to boost China's exports, solar has become a new driving force for China's economy and also contributes to global energy transition. Meanwhile, intensified competition brought by changes in supply and demand, accelerated technical iteration, high interest rates in some regions, and geopolitical tensions caused some volatility in the global PV market, which tested all industry players. We believe that we, as the industry leader, will become even stronger as the competition intensifies.
At the end of Q3, we became the first module manufacturer in the world to have delivered a total of 190GW solar modules, covering over 190 countries and regions. Our capabilities in globalized sales, operations, and management, added by continuous R&D accumulation and innovation, help us build an all-round competition barrier. We are confident in our ability to navigate through the volatility in a cycle, achieve healthy and sustainable profitability, and increase our shareholders' values.
Li Xiande
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
[Non-English content]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
By the end of the third quarter, the mass-produced efficiency of N-type cell reached 25.6%, and the N-type module power output was 25 to 30 watts higher than similar P-type modules. Demand for these products continued to increase globally as the LCOE is lower. N-type modules still retained a premium over similar P-type modules, and the premium continued to exceed the market's average. At the end of the third quarter, we already had over 55GW of N-type cell production capacity. By the end of this year, N-type cell production capacity is expected to reach about 70GW. A competitive capacity structure leading the industry. Recently, our integrated project in Shanxi, China, started construction. Phase one and phase two for a total of 28GW wafer, cell, and module integrated capacity are expected to start production in H1 2024.
In addition, we are optimistic about the growth potential brought by solar storage parity in the long run. Our capacity build-up and development of energy storage business are progressing steadily. Recently, our high efficiency 182 N-type TOPCon cell set a new record with maximum lab conversion efficiency of 26.89%. Again, creating an important milestone in the innovation of our products and the solutions. Thanks to our leadership in driving N-type TOPCon technology, N-type TOPCon products is expected to capture market share greater than 70% in the whole industry, achieving absolute dominance. With higher conversion efficiency, lower industrialization costs and other advantages, we firmly believe TOPCon technology will remain the mainstream technical path for now and in the future 3 to 5 years.
We are confident to be ahead of the industry dynamically by about half a year in terms of power output, cost, and product competitiveness through continuous technology iteration and leveraging our integrated capacity. As a responsible global company, we continue to make progress in sustainable development. With excellent performance in corporate social responsibility, we received a high rating from EcoVadis, outperforming the mainstream PV companies. VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Yeah.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
I randomly check with some customers. I won't say that's 100%, but I checked some key clients of us. Most of them, their feedback is positive. For the existing projects, even if their financial is closed, normally they secure a fixed interest rate across the whole life cycle of their projects, investment cycles. For them, it's safe. Even with the module price coming down and they have more, let's say, returns for their investments or the interest rate doesn't hurt that part.
For the ongoing projects, because even the interest rate is higher and most of the clients can pass the majority of the higher interest rate cost to the end customers, to the PPA customers who can sign a more attractive PPA price than before. Definitely that won't be 100%. I share that point from the customer feedback.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thank you. That's definitely part of the some of the cases may happen. Thank you. I think my final question will be in relation to what is your view on what is the progress of your US expansion capacity, and what is your view as of now as to the chance of getting the IRA subsidies? Because there has been quite a lot of market chatter as to there are some lobbying happening in Washington, et cetera, to target against Chinese players. Would like to know, do you have an update on those?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
We are waiting for this detailed guidance, official detailed guidance release as well. I think it's still not finalized yet, so we are waiting for that as well. For the US market, we believe that's a very promising market. We're still holding our bullish positions on that, and we are trying to do whatever we can to serve the US market. We will take more actions once all these details get released.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Understood. Your plant will complete by the end of this year, right?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
We will see. The previous plans stick to what we have. If your question is regarding whether we have new plans, we have to wait until the detailed guidance release.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Okay. Your plant in Jacksonville, 1GW plant, will be completed on time, right? Disregarding the guidelines.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Yes. Yes.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Okay. Thank you. Thanks a lot.
Operator
At this time, we will conclude our question and answer session. For any additional questions, please contact ir@jinkosolar.com. The conference has now concluded. We thank you for attending today's presentation, and you may now disconnect your lines.

content.text:
Operator
Hello, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for standing by for JinkoSolar Holding Co, Ltd Q2 2023 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the meeting over to your host for today's call, Ms. Stella Wang, JinkoSolar's Investor Relations.
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
Thank you, operator. Thank you, everyone, for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q2 2023 Earnings Conference Call. The company's results were released early today and are available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on newswire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer of JinkoSolar Holding Co, Ltd; Mr. Gener Miao, Chief Marketing Officer of JinkoSolar Co, Ltd; Mr. Pan Li, Chief Financial Officer of JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd, and Mr. Charlie Cao, Chief Financial Officer of JinkoSolar Co, Ltd.
Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and the company's highlights, followed by Mr. Miao, who will talk about the sales and marketing, and then Mr. Pan Li, who will go through the financials. They will all be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor Provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements, except as required under the applicable law. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
We are pleased to report solid growth as we overcame volatility in supply chain prices and end demand. Thanks to our excellent market network, the high quality products, and our highly effective supply chain management. Module shipments in Q2 were approximately 17.8 GW, up 36.2% sequentially. Shipments of the competitive N-type module were approximately 10.4GW, up 74.1% sequentially. We are happy and proud to be the first module manufacturer to reach the milestone of shipping 10GW of N-type modules in a single quarter. Besides, our shipments to the US market increased from Q1, largely reducing demurrage charges. Our efforts in supply chain management, technology advancement, and process improvement also improved our profitability. Net income was $180.1 million in Q2, up 65.6% sequentially.
Adjusted net income was $196.7 million, up 70.5% sequentially. Diluted earnings per ordinary share were $0.77, up 48.5% sequentially.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
Due to the substantial release of polysilicon production volumes and excessive inventory, polysilicon prices declined sharply in Q2, which also caused a certain volatility in module prices. Since most customers are sensitive to price, they were cautious and slowed down their orders, which to some extent affected our module demand. As the lower supply chain prices stabilized in Q3, domestic customers started to place orders, and major projects were initiated and started construction in China. The lower prices also led to a surge in demand from some overseas markets. We expect production and sales in the PV market to rebound in H2.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
With more and more players deploying TOPCon production capacity, N-type TOPCon is certain to become the mainstream technology in the industry. However, some of the new entrants experienced product delays and slower-than-expected production and efficiency ramp up due to insufficient technical know-how and differences in technology and the process, keeping competitive N-type production in short supply. As of the end of Q2, the mass-produced efficiency of our 182 N-type TOPCon capacity had reached 25.5%. This N-type module power output of around 580W peak, which is about 25W to 30 peak more than P-type modules of the same variant. The integrated cost of N-type module remains competitive compared to P-type modules. We are confident we will continue to lead in efficiency and cost through technology iteration and process optimization.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
At the end of May, we announced the construction of a major production base of 66GW integrated wafer cell module capacity in Shanxi, which will become the largest N-type integrated production facility in the industry. Our Shanxi integrated base is another strategic expansion of the production model championed by JinkoSolar in the PV industry that will fully demonstrate our core advantages in highly efficient technology and products, lower investment costs, and greater operational efficiency, as well as intelligent and smart manufacturing capabilities. Meanwhile, we proactively responded to shifts in the global PV landscape by expanding our overseas industrial chain.
The 1GW capacity expansion for N-type modules in the US is expected to start production in September this year. So far, we have established an industry-leading overseas industrial chain network with integrated production capabilities from wafer, cell, to module with traceability and excellent product competitiveness.
As we continue to invest in N-type capacity expansion overseas in the H2, we will reach an integrated capacity of over 12GW overseas by the end of 2023, with N-type accounting for over 75%. We will continuously strengthen and expand our global industrial chain to provide premium and high-quality products and services to our global clients.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
As one of the largest and most innovative solar module manufacturers in the world, we have always carried on social responsibility and taken a continuous improvement of our ESG management as a key matter for our sustainable development. In Q2, we set up a goal and a roadmap to net zero emissions based on methods and requirements advised by the Science Based Targets initiative, SBTi, actively promoting our global carbon emissions reduction and addressing climate change with concrete actions. With outstanding performance in social responsibility fulfillment, we led the mainstream PV industry in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment. We improved our traceability system and independent third party audit mechanism to enhance our supply chain reliability.
Meanwhile, we also enhanced our cooperation with leading institutions and professionals in global renewable energy development and joined the International Renewable Energy Agency, IRENA.
Through sharing best practices and experience, we are dedicated to making a positive contribution to the sustainable advancement of renewable energy globally.
Xiande Li
Chairman of the Board and CEO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
[Foreign Language]
Stella Wang
Head of Investor Relations, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
In summary, we are confident in the development of the PV industry. We will continue to enhance our integrated operations and management. We are positive about the long-term prospect of PV plus energy storage model and will continue to grow our competitiveness by actively developing our energy storage business. Before turning over to Gener, I would like to go over our guidance for the Q3 and the full year of 2023. By the end of 2023, we expect to mass produce the N-type cell efficiency to reach 25.8%. We are optimistic that demand will grow as industrial chain prices stabilize and reach our full-year module shipments to be in the range of 70GW to 75GW.
With N-type module accounting for approximately 60% of the total module shipments. As demand for N-type products continues to increase in the global market, we will move on to invest in N-type capacity, which is competitive both in technology and cost. We expect our annual production capacity for mono wafers, solar cells, and solar modules to reach 85GW, 90GW, and 110GW respectively by the end of 2023. This N-type capacity accounting for over 75% of the total capacity. We expect the module shipments to be in the range of 19GW to 21GW for Q3 2023.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Thank you, Miss Li. Total shipments in Q2 were around 18.6GW, over 95% of which were module shipments. We are glad that total module shipment in H1 2023 exceeds 30GW, making us the number one in the PV industry for the H1 module shipment. In terms of product mix, N-type Tiger Neo accounted for 58% of the module shipments in Q2, a steady increase from nearly 50% in the previous quarter, thanks to its high power output, quality, and reliability. In terms of geographic mix, China and Europe remained the largest regions in Q2, accounting for over 50% together. The proportions of other markets remain relatively stable.
Most importantly, we are glad and proud to see both the efficiency of customs clearance and the size of our shipment to the US market improve sequentially, benefiting from our dedicated efforts. As we continue to make effective progress, we expect our shipments to the US market to gradually increase in H2. For orders and prices, visibility of our order book has reached about 80% for the whole year of 2023, improving compared with Q1, with overseas orders making the majority. Decline in raw material prices drove module price lower. Recent prices for our new contracts have fluctuated within a reasonable range in line with market trends. Tiger Neo retains a competitive premium over P-type. With the gradual release of our N-type capacity, we expect the Tiger Neo to accelerate its penetration into China, Europe, and emerging markets in H2.
The proportion of Tiger Neo shipment for the full year 2023 to reach around 60% of our total module shipments and its product strengths to continue to lead the industry. Recently, we were awarded the Top Brand PV Europe Seal 2023 by EUPD Research. This recognition by our downstream partners does not only prove that JinkoSolar is one of the preferred European brand for installers to work with but also reflect our strong reputation and the commitment to our customers as a leading supplier and the N-type TOPCon technology leader. In addition, we are recognized as 2023 Overall Highest Achiever for the first consecutive year in Renewable Energy Test Center PV Module Index Report, a reaffirmation of quality, bankability, and the reliability of our product.
In summary, we are happy to navigate through volatility in supply chain prices and end demand in Q2, leveraging our advantage in terms of global marketing network, industrial chain layout, and product competitiveness. Meanwhile, we continued to improve our mechanism to cope with risks and enhance our customer relations and marketing network. As supply chain prices stabilized recently, we are optimistic about the return of demand in the global market for H2. In the medium and the long term, as the economy of solar power becomes more and more prominent, the PV market will move forward at a healthy and sustainable growth pace. We expect China, the US, Europe, and other developed markets to grow at a steady pace and the emerging markets will continuously expand in size.
We are confident we will provide more economic value to our customers with excellent products and services, and continue to grow our market share. With that, I will turn the call to Pan.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
Thank you, Gener. We're pleased to report strong financial results in Q2, with quarterly total revenues, gross profit, income from operations, and net income all reaching historical new high. Recently, our majority-owned principal operating subsidiary, JinkoSolar Co, Ltd, announced its intention to issue ordinary shares for no more than RMB 9.6 billion to fund the construction of our N-type integrated production facility in Shanxi. This expansion of advanced integrated production capacity will help us to continuously improve our cost structure, and increasing equity capital will also help us improve our capital structure. As we keep enhancing our global industrial chain, marketing network, and product competitiveness, we hope to achieve healthy and sustainable profitability. Let me go into more details now. Total revenue was over RMB 4.2 billion, up 32% sequentially and up 63% year-over-year.
Gross margin was 15.6% compared to 14.7% in the Q2 last year. We continue to make good progress in clearing customs in the US market, significantly reducing demurrage charges compared with the Q1 this year. Total operating expenses accounted for 11% of total revenues compared with 12% in the Q1 this year and 16% in the Q2 last year, improving sequentially and year-over-year. Income from operations was $212 million, compared with income from operations of $176 million in the Q1 this year and loss from operations of $43 million in the Q2 last year, improving sequentially and year-over-year. Operating margin was about 5% flat compared with the Q1 this year, and loss margin of 1.5% in the Q2 last year, also improving year-over-year.
Net income attributable to JinkoSolar Holdings ordinary shareholders was about $180 million, up 66% sequentially and compared to a net loss attributable to the JinkoSolar Holdings ordinary shareholders of about $93 million, improving year-over-year. Excluding the impact from a change in fair value of notes, a change in fair value of long-term investments, and share-based compensation expenses, adjusted net income attributable to the ordinary shareholders was about $197 million, up about 71% sequentially and up 2.9x year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share was $0.77 in Q2, up about 49% sequentially and compared to diluted loss per share of $0.47 in Q2 last year, improving year-over-year. Moving to the balance sheet.
At the end of Q2, our cash and cash equivalents were about CNY 2.35 billion, up from CNY 1.48 billion at the end of Q1 this year, improving sequentially. Accounts receivable turnover days for 79 days compared with 95 days in Q1. Inventory turnover days decreased to 17 days in Q2 from 100 days in Q1. Total debt was CNY 4.7 billion at the end of Q2, compared to CNY 4.4 billion at the end of Q1. Net debt was CNY 2.4 billion compared to CNY 2.9 billion at the end of Q1 this year. This concludes our prepared remarks. We're now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel you request, please press star two. If you are on a speakerphone, please pick up the handset to ask your question.
Operator
The first question today comes from Brian Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
[Analyst] (Goldman Sachs)
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Hi. Thanks for taking the questions. This is Grace on for Brian. I guess first question around ASP trajectory. Obviously, polysilicon had a big decline in Q2, though it has stabilized in recent week. At the same time, like, we're hearing some oversupply in certain areas of the market. Just wonder if you can talk about the ASP and maybe the margin trajectory moving through the rest of the year and maybe into 2024. Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
This is Charlie speaking. Firstly, I want to talk, this year it's a very big solar market. A lot of markets are very strong, including China, United States, and European markets. We delivered a very strong performance for H1. In terms of revenue shipments, the next generation N-type TOPCon, we are leading the industry and take about 50% market share. Now 50% of portfolios is from N-type. We believe we are continuing the momentum throughout the year.
One time, because of the cutting edge and it's a very strong, great functions for end customers and have advanced more power output for the end customer. We are seeing the market is accepting the N-type, it's going to dominate the markets and will continue the supply relatively shortage even throughout next year. Back to questions on ASP, the H1, it's pretty relatively stable. Starting from June this year, because of the polysilicon, relatively oversupply situations and make the solar modules have the relatively adjustments.
It's if you're looking for the midterm perspective, we think it's very good for the downstream and accelerate the demands from different markets. It will also generate solar and storage the big markets in the future. For the ASP trend, it's relatively in line with the industry. H2 it's for sure in the downward trend, but it's like it has been stabilized. We believe, thanks to the very strong China installations, particularly in Q4 this year, the ASP will maintain and maybe possibly, you know, relatively in upward trends.
For the proper margins profitability's, I just said we strongly believe and we almost closed out the sales order this year, and over 80% is booked. So we are planning, actually for the next year. For this year, we believe the momentum will continue and year over year it's a very good year for Jinko, in terms of the profitability, even the H2. The N-type will take, more shipments for Jinko H2, 60% to 65%, which is 50% in the H1. On top of that, US market is very positive for us starting from Q3.
Our modules was detained starting from last year. We have do a lot of work, feasibilities, ESGs and communications with relevant US regulators. Starting from July, our modules and the speed of the, let's say, going through the customs has been speed up and we are expecting our shipments to US market will be accelerated starting this Q3. We have also get ready for the overseas capacities, 12GW integrated, starting from wafer to modules and to for the US market next year. Next year will be a very big mark year for Jinko to have the more market share in the US.
As well as we have been in expansion for the US module capacities, 1GW is in place, and we plan to start operations from this end of Q3. That's back to your questions overall.
[Analyst] (Goldman Sachs)
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thanks, Charlie. That's super. Maybe I missed it. Can you provide us your updated CapEx number for 2023? Also you talked about like 12GW for overseas capacity next year. Just wondering if you can provide us the CapEx number and how you're thinking about funding it, because I think you mentioned like these, the equity that or the capital that you raise in China cannot be used in the US. Just wonder how you think about the capital raise here. Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Yes. You know, for the CapEx this year, it's roughly RMB 15 billion. We estimate, you know, H1 we have generated around roughly, let's say, RMB 5.5 billion operating cash flows. This year, we estimate over RMB 10 billion operating cash flows this year. As well as we have completed the convertible loans in a certain quarter in a year. So we have sufficient cash to support the CapEx. Next year the overseas capacities almost we will complete it by the end of this year. So we don't foresee any additional cash needs next year for the 12GW integrated capacities.
[Analyst] (Goldman Sachs)
Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Thank you. I'll take the rest offline.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Thank you.
Operator
The next question comes from Philip Shen with Roth MKM. Please go ahead.
Matt Casamassima
Managing Director, ROTH MKM
This is Matt on for Phil. Thanks for taking the questions. Looking at the US market, there is this expectation in the industry that modules made with Chinese poly that was not from Xinjiang could get into the US, but we haven't really been seeing that yet. Do you know what might be taking so long and when non-Xinjiang Chinese poly modules made in Southeast Asia might get cleared by CBP?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Yes. For Jinko, we focus on 100% polysilicon out of China to serve the US markets. Just like I said we are very pretty smooth and speed up the process starting from Q3. For the China-based poly and the probabilities of the, you know, we're not sure, but it's possible, but from Jinko perspective, we will continue. We have signed long-term contract with the Tier 1 and the poly makers out of China, and we will continue to increase the, you know, the source and the volume from the poly producers.
The poly out of China the volume is roughly 10,000 metric tons, which we believe is sufficient to supply the US market. As Tier 1 companies, we can take the advantage. We have the largest integrated capacity, 12GW including 75% TOPCon, you know, the N-type. I think we can take the lead in terms of the market share as well as the poly sourcing from the suppliers out of China.
Matt Casamassima
Managing Director, ROTH MKM
Do you think it's possible that non-China poly, not made in Xinjiang ever makes it into the US? I'm just kind of curious on your view.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
I'm not in a position to make the predictions or the judgment. From the legal perspective, the treatability and if you can do, you know. From the implementation perspective from the relevant regulators, we are not sure their positions.
Matt Casamassima
Managing Director, ROTH MKM
Okay. Thank you for the color. I'll pass it along.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Thank you.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. The next question comes from Rajiv Chaudhri with Sunsara Capital. Please go ahead.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Good morning and good evening. First of all, congratulations on a superb quarter and for the very strong guidance. One question that has not been asked yet and is about the inventory reserve that you have taken in the quarter. Normally your inventories tend to go up every quarter because you are growing the business. They grow up by $200 million to $250 million a quarter. This time your inventories sequentially were down about $200 million, quarter to quarter. My first question is it reasonable to think that the inventory reserve that you took was actually in the neighborhood of $400 million?
Which would make sense given the sharp decline in the prices of poly and obviously at any point in time, you have a lot of poly in your work in process. So, the first question is the inventory reserve in the ballpark of $350 million or $400 million, and that your gross margin without this inventory reserve would actually be in the mid-20s in Q2?
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
Yes. Hello, Rajiv, this is Pan.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Yes.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
As you mentioned to the inventory reserve, yes, actually, we made some inventory reserve in the Q2. This also impacted our gross margin. This is only a temporary treatment of the inventory. We don't think it will be a long-term treatment to our inventory.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
I understand that, Pan. Obviously it's a one-time thing. The question is, was it in the ballpark of $400 million? If the reserve was not taken, your true earnings would be $400 million higher.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You mean RMB 400 million is one number. It's we provided roughly, I think, RMB 500 million inventory provisions. Q2, I think we do pretty good. We anticipated, let's say, the poly decline starting from June. We speed up the inventory goods delivery and control the inventories very tight. That is why you are seeing our total inventory, the numbers is relatively lower quarter-over-quarter. We still have some kind of the orders and targeting the residential markets.
Residential markets, it's kind of the distributor customers, and they are typically, when the supply chain, particularly the end price, has a significant, let's say, adjustment, which we typically will offer some price discounts to the residential customers. That is why from the accounting perspective, by the end of Q2, we recorded additional inventory one-time provisions. We don't believe that is recurring items in the future.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Charlie, I understand it is not an ongoing thing. My question simply is reflecting what was the true earning power of the company in Q2? What I'm trying to get at is that if the poly, if you exclude the impact that the sharp decline in poly prices has had on the, on the inventory reserve, that your earnings would have been a lot higher. Not just somewhat higher, but a lot higher, maybe as much as $400 million higher.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You mean if let's say the poly price has relatively stabilized and the module price is relatively stable. For sure, if that is the case, and we are able to generate more earnings, significantly.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Is it fair to say that without this inventory reserve, the gross margin could have been in the mid-20s, 24%, 25%?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Well, I think it is roughly, I think, without that, it's roughly up to 20%.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
You expect it to be higher in Q3 because the rate at which the price of modules is coming down is slower than the rate at which the poly price is coming down.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
We expect strong, continuously strong earnings, because the N-type modules they have strong earning generation power. We get more percentage shipments. Secondly, we have higher shipments in the US markets. That is a combination of the two key factors. Of course, the poly is down to be stabilized. Module is still reaching kind of the stabilized forms.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Also, my next question is about the storage business. Did the storage business contribute any revenues in Q2? What should we expect for the full year?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Yes. Storage is from long-term perspective, kind of the with flex it's got going to be a very big, very important business unit from the long term three to five years. This year is a kind of investment year. We invest on the teams, sales channels and R&D, even we still invest some small capacities. The revenue contribution for this year is not significant, and we even make some, we are expecting, this year from an investment year. We will make some kind of small losses for the business. For the future, it's looking to the next year. It's going to be a very big, let's say high growth segment for Jinko.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Will you hit a few hundred million dollar this year or not really?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
No. This year, I think, you know, maybe I think, but we don't disclose the numbers. But again, it's kind of the early investment, segment, the business unit. But we have roughly reached our workforce, sizable teams, including the key functions, by the end of this Q4. We think we are in a good position and for next year, you know, to penetrate the storage markets.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Right. Also, going back to the cost of polysilicon, is it fair to think that the average cost of the polysilicon in Q2 was roughly $0.03 lower than the cost of polysilicon that you had in Q1?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Sorry, could you repeat your question?
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
My question is on the cost of polysilicon. I'm talking not about the cost of polysilicon in the market, but the cost of polysilicon that you embedded in your earnings in your operations and therefore your earnings. Is it fair to think that the cost of polysilicon in Q2, excluding the inventory reserve was roughly $0.03 lower than the Q1 cost of polysilicon?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
I didn't have the numbers. I know your questions. Q1, I think, you know, the poly starting January is a kind of very big rebound and slightly down month over month and significant decline starting from June. I think it's, starting in June, it's a small impact on the Q2 financial figures because we have the inventory turnover is 60 days, 20 days. We can get back to you know, after the call. I think it's slightly lower, you know, the poly from the financial statement perspective, Q2, which is Q1.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Also, one last question. Is it fair to say that at this point in Q3, your average cost, your total cost, per watt is under $0.15?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You know, we don't disclose the numbers. It's a kind of competitive, you know, advantage and let's say information. You know, it's a significant improvement back to your questions in Q3 starting from July, as well as we continue to improve our internal operations versus the supply chain the cost. It's a significant improvement. We don't disclose the cost structure, even including the total direct costs.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Right. Final question, Charlie. You know, First Solar has made a point of noting that they have a lot of long-term contracts going out multiple years, going out two, three, four years, and Maxeon has said the same thing. These contracts are for prices in the high twenties going out multiple years. Do you think that kind of pricing that far out is really sustainable given what is actually happening to prices in the market right now?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
I think US market generally is a very big market, sustainable long growth. There are a lot of disruptions from the recent two years because of the, let's say the WRO, UFLPA, so makes the supply, you know, tight. So some of the, let's say the local producers takes that advantage, sign a lot of long-term contract. From the long-term perspective, we still, the silicon-based technology has the absolute 100% advantage versus other technology. So now it's, the focus is, overseas polysilicon supply relative shortage. We are able to, let's say, next year we're, it's going to be a very big year for Jinko.
We have secured sufficient poly out of China. So we are able to sign very decent contracts. With let's say the policy stabilized and we are able to get more contracts out only next year, maybe next two or three years. Historically, we take the majority of very big market share in US, 20% to 25%, because of disruptions, but we have overcome the disruptions. So for the long term, we think we are in good positions with our peers.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Final question. Will you be able to take advantage of the IRA in terms of the production that you are starting with the 1GW N-type of product in the US?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
The only IRA, you know. You mean if Jinko is applicable or not? We think the IRA is kind of very transparent in our policies, and it's for the local productions in the US. But when we do that, we don't, let's say, depend on 100% IRA. We think relatively sized local productions and local content makes Jinko the more competitive in the market. But we strongly believe the IRA is. We are qualified, let's say the IRA.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Okay. You expect that you will be able to benefit from it, but you're not counting on it?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
We do very conservative accounting. I know some peers the US producers, they do accrual basis, even they record it on the cost of goods sold. You know, that's a different accounting perspective. We didn't do that. We want to do it on cash basis based on the application and the result of the IRA in future.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and CEO, Sunsara Capital
Okay. Thank you, and congratulations again.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Thank you.
Operator
As a reminder, if you wish to ask a question, please press star then one to enter the question queue. Once again, if you have a question, please press star then one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. The next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies. Please go ahead.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thanks for taking my question and congratulation for the great results. A couple of questions to follow up. First of all, I would like to clarify. The amount. Because, in Asia reporting the overall impairment in Q2 was around RMB 1.6 billion. In US reporting, around RMB 500 million is recorded in cost of revenue, and the remaining is under the impairment of long-lived assets. Is this understanding correct?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You're right. It's a kind of different presentations in different, you know, the accounting standards. In the US, the inventory provisions is typically an item of cost of goods sold. In China, the PRC standards, they have separate line called kind of assets impairment, including everything the fixed assets and as well as the inventories. That's a kind of the presentation different, accounting standards.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
If we add back RMB 500 million of inventory impairment, the gross margin in Q2 was actually improving compared to Q1, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Yes, you're right.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Another thing is, the impairment of long life assets to my understanding are those equipment which we can also expect it as a one-off thing, right? Because the impairment of equipment won't happen every quarter.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
It's a one-off, and we provided for the small size and small size module cell capacities. You know, we to make our assets to be more competitive on the balance sheets.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thank you. Another question is in relation to the port charges, because I recall that in Q4 last year and Q1 this year, there were port charges affecting the market. What is the situation of the port charges in the US in Q2, and what do you expect in Q3 with the acceleration in the clearance of the products?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You know, for the port charges and in Q1, we have RMB 400 million in port charges. For the US, because it's detained modules and very high storage costs. Q2 increased a lot to RMB 200 million only in one quarter. But starting from Q3, we believe, you know, the port charges will be a very small numbers, and because our modules have been cleaned up and speed up on the US customs side.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thanks a lot. This is an exciting development actually. It leads to the next question as to how much US shipment has been sold to the US in Q1 and Q2?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You mean the shipments percentage, right?
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Yes.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
The US shipments against the total shipments. It's 5% to 10% in that range.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Understood. For this year, after we raise our guidance to 70GW to 75GW, 5% to 10% is around like four to 7GW. Next year our target is 12GW. Is it correct?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
You know, it's roughly 10% of market shipment next year. It could be in the range, let's say above 10GW. Depending on let's say particularly the supply side the poly side. But we are confident 10GW is a kind of the base case.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Base case, right. Thank you. That's actually quite a strong improvement from this year, like 4GW to 7GW to 10GW still. Would like to know what is your expectation on US installation next year on this basis? Because this year probably, US, I think the base case is like around 30GW. I think the company is implying market share gain next year, right?
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
It's kind of a go back to normal strategy, right? In the last two years' time, let's say we got stuck by different regions. As of now, we have seen, you know, positively, you know, things go back, start to go back to normal. That's why we are expecting a kind of normal market share or normal stable supply from JinkoSolar to US market. That's why we expect, you know, around 10% of our total shipment goes to US market next year.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
What is your expectation on US installation in 2024 then, like approximately?
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd
Well, it depends. It's really we see a robust demand there. It's really a question of whether the supply will be normal or it will be, let's say, strictly under the UFLPA inspection, right?
That will decide what could be the size of the US market. It could be somewhere from 30GW to even up to 50GW. It really depends on the supply side.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thank you. My last question is basically for the polysilicon supply correspondingly. Because 12GW approximately you still need quite a lot of polysilicon, like probably around like 20,000 to 30,000 tons. Have you locked in that supply already?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Majority of product we have locked. The overseas capacity is 100,000 metric tons, which can support, let's say, you know, I think roughly 50GW. We take 20% market share from the, let's say, the poly supply side. We are as confident. As well as some of the overseas capacity, we still have some flexibility to increase the capacity. We're thinking, you know, we can achieve that.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Thanks a lot. I've got a final question on A-share placement. Will that eventually lead to dilution of the US shareholding?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Yes. If you know, it's probably maybe 7% to 9% dilutions, but it's not significant. We take you know the US you know has 58% you know the shareholding of the A-share. If let's assume 10%, you know, the maximum, maybe it should be lower. It's roughly 53%, right? 5%, you know, the difference, the lower.
Alan Lau
VP of Equity Research, Jefferies
Understood. Thanks a lot for taking my question, and congratulations again for the great results. Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Co Ltd
Thank you.
Operator
This does conclude our question and answer session and our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
